title: Capacity of parallel Gaussian channels via water-filling

problemStatement.formal: For noise powers N_1,...,N_n > 0 and budget P >= 0, max_{P_i >= 0, sum P_i <= P} sum_i (1/2) log(1 + P_i/N_i) = sum_i (1/2) log(1 + P_i*/N_i), attained by the water-filling allocation P_i* = (mu - N_i)_+ where the water level mu >= 0 is the unique solution of sum_i (mu - N_i)_+ = P.
problemStatement.plain: Given several independent noisy channels with noise levels N_i and a fixed total transmit power P to share among them, how should the power be split to maximise total data rate? The optimal answer is water-filling: pour power into a landscape whose floor heights are the noise levels until it reaches a common surface level mu, giving each channel power (mu - N_i)_+ and starving channels too noisy to be worth using. The task is to prove this allocation is optimal and that mu is uniquely fixed by the power budget.
whyMatters: Water-filling is the canonical resource-allocation result of information theory and underlies practical multicarrier bit-loading (OFDM/DMT) in DSL, Wi-Fi and 4G/5G.
It is the multi-channel completion of the scalar Shannon-Hartley formula already in the gallery, and formalising it exercises constrained concave (KKT/Lagrange) optimisation in Lean.

proven: Per-use AWGN capacity (1/2) log(1 + P/N) nats/use, verified axiom-free (gallery: shannon-channel-coding-awgn).
Bandlimited Shannon-Hartley C = B log2(1 + P/N) bits/s and its structural theory (gallery: shannon-channel-coding-awgn-oq-03), which explicitly defers this parallel-channel case.
The water-filling theorem is classical (Shannon 1949; Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory, Thm 9.9.1); only the Lean formalization is open.
open: A Lean 4 proof that P_i* = (mu - N_i)_+ maximises the parallel-channel rate under sum P_i <= P.
Existence and uniqueness of the water level mu solving sum_i (mu - N_i)_+ = P.
The closed-form optimum C = sum_i (1/2) log(max(mu, N_i)/N_i).
knownResults.goal: Formalize the finite-dimensional water-filling theorem: define the parallel-channel rate over a finite family N_1,...,N_n, prove existence/uniqueness of the water level, prove KKT optimality of P_i* = (mu - N_i)_+, and derive the closed-form capacity. Scope is the finite optimisation statement; the continuous infinite-band limit is a separate follow-up.

insights: Water-filling KKT optimality has a fully ELEMENTARY proof: the first-order condition is replaced by the per-channel tangent bound log u <= u-1 (Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos), summed across channels. No differentiability/Lagrange/KKT machinery needed.

Key identity N_i + (mu-N_i)_+ = max mu N_i turns the derivative coefficient 1/(2(N_i+P_i*)) into 1/(2 max(mu,N_i)), which is constant 1/(2mu) on ACTIVE channels (N_i<mu) and <= 1/(2mu) on inactive ones (P_i*=0, x_i>=0). This case split is exactly what makes the aggregated linear term collapse to (sum x_i - P)/(2mu) <= 0.

Water level existence = IVT on the continuous monotone budget g(mu)=sum (mu-N_i)_+ between g(0)=0 and g(N_{i0}+P)>=P; uniqueness (for P>0) = strict monotonicity of g wherever g>0 (some channel active).
